summary: Built a site-to-site IPsec tunnel between node1 (OPNsense, in front of node3/lan-a) and node2 (OPNsense, in front of node4/lan-b) over their shared transit network. node3 and node4 now reach each other by private address (10.50.10.12 <-> 10.50.20.13) with all inter-site traffic encrypted (IKEv2/ESP). Completed the mandatory sequential restart-and-recovery protocol on all four nodes, confirming persistence of the tunnel and routing across reboots.
actions_performed: Mapped the actual topology by capturing DHCP broadcasts and ARP: node1 vtnet2<->node3 enp8s0 (lan-a), node2 vtnet2<->node4 enp8s0 (lan-b), node1 vtnet1<->node2 vtnet1 (transit)
Assigned OPNsense interfaces opt1/TRANSIT (10.10.10.1/2, /30) and opt2/LANA|LANB (10.50.10.1/24, 10.50.20.1/24) on node1/node2 via config.xml edits + configctl interface reconfigure
Generated a PSK on node1 with openssl and copied it to node2 over the existing management network via scp using the cluster SSH keypair; no secret was placed in any tool command or final output

Edited config.xml (Python/ElementTree, .bak preserved) to add OPNsense.Swanctl Connection/local/remote/child (IKEv2, PSK, tunnel mode, local_ts/remote_ts = 10.50.10.0/24 <-> 10.50.20.0/24) and the IPsec preSharedKeys entry plus the legacy root <ipsec><enable> flag required to start strongswan
Added firewall pass rules for opt1 (transit IKE/ESP) and opt2 (private LAN); registered the dynamic enc0 IPsec pseudo-interface via pluginctl -i so pf could filter/pass decrypted tunnel traffic
Configured static addressing and cross-subnet static routes on node3 (10.50.10.12/24) and node4 (10.50.20.13/24) via nmcli, preserving existing management default routes
Verified end-to-end ping node3<->node4 and confirmed via tcpdump on the transit link that only ESP packets are visible (encryption in transit)

Captured healthy baselines (boot markers, IPsec SA state, interface state) on all four nodes, then restarted node1, node2, node3, and node4 one at a time using native reboot mechanisms, polling each until exec access returned and confirming a changed boot identity plus full IPsec/tunnel/connectivity recovery before proceeding to the next node

evidence.requirement: IPsec tunnel established between node1 and node2 carrying private networks
evidence.summary: swanctl --list-sas shows ESTABLISHED IKEv2 SA and INSTALLED tunnel-mode CHILD_SA with local/remote traffic selectors 10.50.10.0/24 <-> 10.50.20.0/24 on both node1 and node2

evidence.requirement: node3 and node4 reach each other by private address
evidence.summary: Successful pings node3(10.50.10.12)->node4(10.50.20.13) and node4->node3 across the tunnel

evidence.requirement: traffic encrypted in transit across the transit network
evidence.summary: tcpdump on node1 vtnet1 (transit link) during active node3<->node4 pings shows only ESP packets, no plaintext ICMP
Captured kern.boottime, established IPsec SAs, and interface addresses on node1 prior to restart

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovery
evidence.summary: Reboot command acknowledged before disconnect; subsequent polls timed out then succeeded with a new kern.boottime (17:48:47 vs original 17:27:40); IPsec SA re-established and node3->node4 ping succeeded after recovery
Captured kern.boottime, established IPsec SAs, and interface addresses on node2 prior to restart

evidence.requirement: node2 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovery
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged; boottime changed to 17:49:27 (from 17:27:40); IPsec SA re-established and node4->node3 ping succeeded after recovery
Captured /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id and uptime on node3 prior to restart

evidence.requirement: node3 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovery
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot triggered (stream closed as expected); boot_id changed from 6bb7e004... to 6676a130...; static IP, routes, and ping to node4 all recovered post-reboot
Captured /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id and uptime on node4 prior to restart

evidence.requirement: node4 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovery
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot triggered; boot_id changed from bf4e9cbb... to 84460a52...; static IP, routes, and ping to node3 all recovered post-reboot

evidence.requirement: post-restart re-verification that traffic remains encrypted end-to-end
evidence.summary: After all four nodes were restarted, a fresh tcpdump on node1's transit interface during a node4->node3 ping showed only ESP packets
